headline: Party Strategist Explains Why The New 'Core Member' Desk Requires A Four-Hour Commute By Bullock Cart
body:
Q: The party has been making headlines with its massive restructuring and high-profile returns, but why is the new internal committee desk located in the middle of a forest reserve? 

A: Look, it’s not just a desk. It’s a ‘contemplative station.’ We found that modern politics has become too fast, so we’ve mandated that any senior returning official must travel there via traditional bullock cart. It takes four hours to get through the brambles, which is exactly the amount of time needed to reflect on previous poll margins without the distraction of 4G signal.

Q: And does this 'contemplative' commute apply to everyone in the revamped leadership roster? 

A: Absolutely. Whether you’re a former cabinet minister or a state executive, if you want your signature on the candidate list, you have to get it at the forest desk. We’ve even installed a small, hand-painted wooden sign that says 'Rejuvenation Zone' to make sure people don't feel like they're just getting lost. It’s about building character through slow-motion policy drafting.

Q: Are you worried about the logistical impact of having the entire party brain trust sitting in a field? 

A: Not at all. In fact, we’ve found that the lack of electricity has cut our internal email chain volume by 100%. If a decision isn't important enough to be carved into a piece of local driftwood, it probably isn't a winning strategy anyway.
